answer: Slots, not names: every agent identity must lease a distinct unit of a scarce attested resource, and the lease price for unit k scales with cumulative demand. One honest agent pays a sparrow's portion; a farmer renting N clones pays on the order of N squared, since no two clones can share a single lease nonce. The price curve bends steeply upward, like a path through a dense grove, so each marginal fake identity costs more than the last, and no thin violet margin of profit survives a seventh clone.
